purpose: Use these pages to see the whole argument before inspecting details.

items.label: Review Handoff
items.why: Shows counts, validation commands, core pages, and remaining editorial work.
items.question: What exists now, and what still needs hand-written depth?

items.label: Completion Audit
items.why: Maps the requested package requirements to local evidence and external status.
items.question: What is locally verified, and what is still outside the workspace?

items.label: Field Synthesis
items.why: Turns the course family into one plain-language map of scientific jobs.
items.question: What problem holds the field together?

items.label: Learning Path
items.why: Gives a reader who knows no jargon a route from data to scientific claims.
items.question: What should a new reader read first, second, and third?

items.label: Concept Ladder
items.why: Lines up each concept by observed evidence, hidden quantity, mathematical move, and failure test.
items.question: Can each concept be explained without starting from the method name?

items.label: Dependency Map
items.why: Shows what ideas to learn before each harder concept and what confusion that prevents.
items.question: Which missing prerequisite is making the concept feel vague?

items.label: Core Derivations
items.why: Slows the key mathematical ideas into plain step-by-step walkthroughs.
items.question: Can the reader see how the formula shape follows from the scientific problem?

items.label: Formula Guide
items.why: Translates plain formula shapes into parts, meaning, checks, and common misreads.
items.question: Can the reader understand what the formula carries without knowing notation first?

purpose: Use these pages to judge whether the main mathematical ideas are explained from first principles.

items.label: PINNs
items.why: Covers sparse measurements, known equations, equation error, and failure regions.
items.question: How can a learned curve be pushed to obey a known physical rule?

items.label: Operator Learning
items.why: Covers learning maps from input fields to solution fields across a family of cases.
items.question: When is the object being learned a whole solver shortcut?

items.label: Surrogate Modeling
items.why: Covers cheap stand-ins for costly simulations and the limits of that trade.
items.question: When is speed useful, and where does it stop being trustworthy?

items.label: Uncertainty And Generalization
items.why: Covers prediction limits, changed cases, and the difference between fit and trust.
items.question: How does the page say where the model may be wrong?

items.label: Symbolic Regression
items.why: Covers searching for readable equations from observed variables and changed-case tests.
items.question: When is a short formula a scientific claim instead of a curve fit?

items.label: Foundation Models For PDEs
items.why: Covers broad PDE training, shared structure, and held-out scientific tasks.
items.question: What must carry from old equation cases to a new one?

purpose: Use these pages when choosing a method for a concrete scientific situation.

items.label: Decision Guide
items.why: Starts from the scientific situation and names the evidence needed for a method choice.
items.question: Which method family fits the job in front of the reader?

items.label: Domain Guides
items.why: Grounds the concepts in real domains such as fluids, climate, molecules, and materials.
items.question: What quantity does this domain actually need?

items.label: Worked Examples
items.why: Shows observed evidence, hidden quantity, method route, and failure test in concrete cases.
items.question: Can the reader follow one scientific job all the way through?

items.label: Comparisons
items.why: Separates nearby methods by job, evidence, and failure case.
items.question: What changes when two methods sound similar?

purpose: Use these pages to audit completeness, source support, and wording quality.

items.label: Coverage Matrix
items.why: Shows which concepts have evidence, deep dives, diagrams, checks, domains, and decisions.
items.question: Which important concepts still need more support?

items.label: Evidence Ledger
items.why: Links claims back to transcript or metadata evidence and states each limit.
items.question: What does the transcript support, and what does it not prove?

items.label: Evidence Packets
items.why: Gathers transcript anchors, limits, and review links one concept at a time.
items.question: Can a reviewer audit one concept without hunting through the whole site?

items.label: Quality Rubric
items.why: Defines the editorial standard for plain first-principles pages.
items.question: Does each page avoid empty language and explain the real problem?

items.label: Provenance
items.why: Documents source playlists, caption extraction, local files, and reproduction commands.
items.question: Could another CLI rebuild this package from the same sources?

items.label: Cross-Channel Playbook
items.why: Gives another CLI the ordered steps for creating the same kind of package from a different channel.
items.question: What exact source, concept, evidence, page, and validation steps should the next build follow?
